summary: Teams of 2-4 students design and develop a website for Marlowby, a subscription service featuring local products from U.S. cities. The website must be visually engaging, easy to navigate, and explain how Marlowby works, including subscription options and featured cities. Teams present their website live and submit a clickable URL, works cited, release forms, and AI documentation by the deadline.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit all the following in one PDF file: Clickable URL to Project (including any necessary login credentials), Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing Team ID cannot be accepted
The team is responsible for securing a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including oneself, whose image or work is used in the project
The team is responsible for citing all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
presubmit_items: Clickable URL to Project (including any necessary login credentials)
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Device loaded with website for presentation
Students may use one single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Apply audience analysis and design principles and elements to create intuitive navigation, engaging content, and effective page layouts using UX/UI best practices, ensuring accessibility and visual appeal across devices and platforms

Assess project requirements and delegate tasks effectively within multidisciplinary teams, utilizing project management tools, agile methodologies, and collaborative workflows to create and maintain high-quality, SEO-optimized site content

Implement accessibility standards (WCAG, ADA), develop responsive designs for multiple devices, integrate search functionality, and incorporate optimized graphics and multimedia elements to enhance usability, engagement, and compliance

Develop web applications using current standards-based languages (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) and implement functionality with modern scripting frameworks (React, Vue) following best practices for performance and security

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.
Team submitted clickable Project URL (with login credentials if needed), Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual and BPA Release Form(s ), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Visual organization is clear and intuitive; colors and fonts are highly aesthetic and enhance readability; consistent format is maintained across all pages.
Graphics strongly enhance the topic; highly creative and original design using templates, code, or both.
Well-developed, comprehensive information; website strongly supports campaign goals.

Website works seamlessly across browsers; source code is clean, organized, and validated; innovative technologies (e.g., SASS, Python, JavaScript) are effectively used; grammar and spelling are flawless.
All links present, fully functional, consistently formatted; navigation path is clear, logical, and easy to follow.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
